title: Governing Paper People | Sovereign Citizens
summary: Knowing Better explains religious, diplomatic and constitutional strains of sovereign citizens and debunks the Articles of Confederation, 14th Amendment, strawman and gold-fringe theories.

assertions.quote: Even if they believe that the government has no power and the laws don't apply to them, the rest of us do.

verdicts.note: The Seventh Circuit holds that whatever status a person claims (sovereign citizen, secured-party creditor, flesh-and-blood human), that person is not beyond the courts' jurisdiction; the defendants' insistence that they did not consent changed nothing and they were tried and convicted.

Schemes that 'defeat or restrict court authority' and 'everything is a contract' are two of the five pseudolaw categories Meads refuted, and that refutation has been adopted by courts across the Commonwealth.
Opting out of government and court authority by withdrawing consent is a Freeman motif; its founder pled guilty to the very offence he claimed immunity from and courts reject it.

NZ courts rejected three habeas and criminal litigants who said a court needs their contract or consent; no one has to consent to a jurisdiction to be subject to it, especially for tax or criminal law.
Claims that government authority needs consent and can be withdrawn unilaterally were refused leave as having no merit; the authors call it a distorted social-contract idea.

assertions.quote: it has no legal meaning. There's no law saying that gold fringe makes it a naval ensign.

verdicts.note: The court reviews flag law: fringe is not part of the flag, has no heraldic or legal significance, and cannot change a court's jurisdiction, which 'is a matter of law, statute, and constitution'. It cites several courts calling the argument frivolous.

assertions.quote: they're not citizens, but nationals, which still makes you subject to the laws of the United States
But again, these aren't mutually exclusive. You are both rather than one or the other.
But none of this matters anyway, because we don't live under the Articles of Confederation.

verdicts.note: The Constitution was ratified in 1788 and replaced the Articles; every court applies it.

assertions.quote: which is why sovereign citizens and tax protest movements often go hand in hand
They've even been labeled as a domestic terrorist movement.
They also employ a number of paper terrorism tactics, including putting false liens on your property.

verdicts.note: The Ninth Circuit affirmed 14 counts and 87 months for false UCC liens against prison staff, and notes a nationwide rise since 2004 in such liens against officials, which led Congress to enact 18 U.S.C. 1521.
Treasury notes that scheme participants file false IRS Forms 8300 and Currency Transaction Reports in the names of law enforcement officials and others they seek to harass.
Adherents file false liens, fake letters of credit and fabricated tax reports against officials ('paper terrorism'); one couple filed $250 billion in liens against a dozen Minnesota officials.
FBI lists frivolous lawsuits and liens against officials' property as harassment tactics, which led Congress to create a federal false-lien offense in 2007.
Review says sovereigns are mostly known for 'paper terrorism': frivolous pseudolegal claims for large sums often aimed at officials they believe wronged them.
Experts in the US, Canada and Germany all report paper terrorism, damage claims and false liens against officials, and harassment of officials.
